Telegram bot: added /importkey <privateKey> [perTxCap] [dailyCap] so
a user can register with a key they already control instead of only
being offered one the bot generates. The bot still signs on their
behalf during use - that part is unavoidable for a chat interface with
no wallet-extension access - but the user now always has their own
copy of the key from the start rather than depending on bot storage
for it. Best-effort deletes the message containing the raw key.

Refactor/detox

fix: use 'link' mode instead of 'login' for wallet connect on profile page

The profile page was using mode='login' which triggered the full auth
flow (connectAndAuth), redirecting to /migrating upon successful wallet
sign-in. Changed to mode='link' which calls connectAndLink — the
correct flow for attaching a wallet to an already-authenticated user.

Also added onLinked callback to re-fetch the profile so the newly linked
wallet address appears immediately.

fix: correct wallet error normalization and remove duplicate code

- Fixed parentheses in `normalizeWalletError` to ensure proper fallback to empty string
- Removed duplicate `connect` function and redundant imports
- Cleaned up formatting and trailing commas for consistency
fix: resolve TypeScript errors in wallet route and useWalletAuth hook

feat: enforce account-type invariant for wallet-based auth

Add `accountType` field to user model to distinguish wallet accounts from Twitter/X and email accounts. On wallet registration, set `accountType: "wallet"`; on Twitter callback, set `accountType: "x"`.

Prevent wallet login for accounts whose `accountType` is not `"wallet"` (e.g., an X account that shares a wallet address). Also block linking a wallet if it already belongs to an X account, consuming the nonce only after validation. This ensures each authentication flow only works with its intended account type.

fix(missions): stop hiding missions from the board by status

The Missions page and Recent Missions only ever selected 'open' and 'completed' rows, but tasks.status takes five values. A mission that got claimed (all slots taken) or submitted for review silently vanished from the board, as did anything the deadline cron closed as 'cancelled'.

Both listing queries now apply no status filter at all — nothing is dropped from the board. "Open Only" remains the one view that filters, and it does so on request.

BountyCard badges every non-open state instead of just completed: claimed -> In progress, submitted -> In review, completed -> Completed, cancelled -> Expired or Cancelled depending on whether the deadline has passed. Only genuinely closed missions are dimmed; in-flight ones keep full opacity.

"Open First" used to work by sorting status descending, which happened to put 'open' above 'completed' alphabetically. That breaks with 'claimed' and 'submitted' in the mix and PostgREST can't express a CASE ranking, so the ordering moves into a stable STATUS_RANK sort in the store.

deadline_passed is derived in the stores rather than in BountyCard because the React compiler rejects reading the clock during render.
